summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with excellent CGM quality: 3995 valid entries, 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate entries, largest gap 65 minutes. Aggregate glucose is 121.6 mg/dL with time in range 86.0 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. The distribution is strongly time-of-day dependent. Local hours 12:00 to 17:00 carry 14.0 to 32.1 percent time above range with a peak hourly mean of 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00, while local hours 18:00 to 03:00 carry the hypoglycemia burden, notably 15.3 percent below range at 19:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00. No carbohydrates were recorded in the whole period: carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min null, and carbohydrates on board 0 in every sampled loop status. All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false. Insulin totals 275.95 U across 655 entries, about 19.7 U per day, against a profile basal of 16.2 U per day, so unannounced correction and UAM dosing supplies the majority of insulin. Dynamic ISF is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor over a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, and the effective sensitivity observed spans 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, crossing the static value near 170 to 190 mg/dL. Insulin on board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U with zero carbohydrates on board. Three GLP-1 doses, one occlusion with pump error, three site changes, two sensor changes and one profile switch fall inside the period, so the underlying sensitivity cannot be treated as stationary.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data are sufficient for hourly and daily pattern work: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicates, cadence 5.0 minutes, coverage 98.7 percent, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, status good. Local time is BST at UTC plus 60 minutes, and hourly_glucose_local is a clean plus one hour shift of hourly_glucose, confirmed because hour_utc 0 at 90.6 mg/dL equals hour_local 1 at 90.6 mg/dL. The AAPS profile is complete with 7 basal, 5 carb ratio, 1 ISF and 3 target segments plus DIA and a full SMB settings block, and profile_context marks it authoritative with historical applicability yes. Profile basal sums to 16.2 U per day, matching the profile switch note that describes 16.2 U per day with a flat ISF. Two cross-checks against loop output: carb ratios quoted by the algorithm match the profile at the 04:00, 08:00, 16:00 and 20:00 segments, while the 00:00 to 04:00 window repeatedly reports 13.3 g per unit against the profile value of 13.0. Effective sensitivity in loop output never equals 56 mg/dL per unit, confirming the flat ISF acts only as a base for Dynamic ISF. The build is customized: reason strings contain Enhanced oref1, UAM Boost 1 and 2, UAM High Boost, prTrial, twin, antBackout and a G3 pre-UAM uncertainty hold, and effective targets appear that are not derivable from the three profile target segments.

Only 40 of 2315 treatments and 24 of 6214 device statuses are included, so the basal versus bolus split of total daily dose cannot be computed. Insulin peak time for free_peak_oref is not exposed, so any Dynamic ISF back-calculation is approximate. Custom branch parameters that visibly alter dosing are absent from decision_inventory.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the commonly cited 4 percent goal, while coefficient of variation 32.6 percent and time in range 86.0 percent are good. Hypoglycemia is clustered, not diffuse: local hour 01:00 at 18.5 percent, 19:00 at 15.3 percent, 00:00 at 11.4 percent, 03:00 at 10.2 percent, 02:00 and 23:00 at 10.1 percent, 18:00 at 7.7 percent and 22:00 at 6.6 percent. Level 2 readings appear on 2026-08-13 around 18:00 to 18:14 local reaching 42 mg/dL, on 2026-08-14 around 19:04 to 19:14 local reaching 41 mg/dL, and on 2026-08-21 at 07:19 local reaching 42 mg/dL. Eight of 14 days had a minimum at or below 55 mg/dL. Hyperglycemia is also clustered at local 14:00 to 17:00 with 22.6 to 32.1 percent above range and at 10:00 with 20.2 percent. Both hypoglycemia clusters follow the two daily peaks, which is an overshoot signature rather than a flat basal surplus. Insulin on board reached 2.23 U, 2.80 U, 4.73 U and 5.935 U in only 24 sampled statuses, always with carbohydrates on board 0, which is large relative to a 16.2 U per day basal. Confounders inside the period are GLP-1 1.25 mg on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20, an occlusion and pump error on 08-19, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, and a profile switch on 08-13.

analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on data_quality. Coverage is adequate, but the total absence of carbohydrate records means meal overshoot cannot be excluded as the hypoglycemia mechanism, so cause attribution is weaker than pattern detection.

The 42 mg/dL value at 07:19 local on 08-21 preceded a sensor change by about two hours, so an end-of-wear artifact cannot be excluded for that single reading.

analysis_steps.findings: Mapped to local hours the basal shape looks misaligned with the observed curve, but this remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated defect. The lowest segment of 0.5 U per hour from 16:00 sits under the highest glucose hours, 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and 148.9 mg/dL at 17:00 with 22.6 percent above range, while the highest evening segment of 0.7 U per hour from 19:00 sits over the worst evening hypoglycemia hour at 15.3 percent below range. Overnight behavior does not look like a flat basal surplus, because mean glucose rises from 90.6 at 01:00 to 106.0 at 04:00 while time below range falls from 18.5 to 3.0 percent, which fits decaying evening insulin on board under a 10-hour DIA. The only reliably fasting-like window is 02:00 to 07:00 local, where means of 99.5 to 106.0 mg/dL are acceptable. Profile targets are 90, 100 from 08:00 and 90 from 23:00 mg/dL, but effective loop targets observed include 80, 84, 86, 87, 90, 96.4, 97, 99, 101, 104, 108 and 116 mg/dL. Some derive from user temporary targets of 135 mg/dL on 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20 and 108 mg/dL on 08-15, yet 80 mg/dL appears specifically on the most aggressive high glucose loops on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21, below the profile floor, and Autosens target adjustment is disabled in both directions. A decisive coupling was identified: SMB caps are expressed in minutes of profile basal, so the profile basal value itself scales automation aggressiveness by hour, and the observed maximum safe basal of 4 U per hour equals max_daily_safety_multiplier 5 times the largest basal of 0.8 U per hour.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal markers, so the 10:00 to 17:00 elevation cannot be separated from unannounced meals. No activity markers for the 17:00 to 19:00 fall. Only 40 sampled treatments, so the full temp basal series is unavailable. The afternoons of 08-17 and 08-18 contain 180-minute SMB blackouts and are excluded. The source of the 80 mg/dL effective target is unidentified.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios are not assessable. With 0 carbohydrate entries over 14 days and carbohydrates on board 0 in every sampled status, no bolus-to-carbohydrate outcome exists, so all five carb ratio segments are unfalsifiable for this period. The only observation is the 13.3 against 13.0 g per unit discrepancy in the 00:00 to 04:00 window. ISF is one flat segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, but Dynamic ISF is enabled at a 70 percent factor with Autosens disabled, so effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, a factor of 4.4, and is strongly glucose dependent: about 124 at 70 mg/dL, 108 to 112 at 84 to 95, 71 to 87 at 120 to 140, 43 to 66 at 147 to 169 and 27.8 to 37.9 at 245 to 262. The curve crosses the static value near 170 to 190 mg/dL, so the algorithm under-responds through the sustained 130 to 163 mg/dL afternoon band and over-responds above roughly 200 mg/dL, requesting 1.98, 2.12 and 2.59 U immediately at those levels. DIA of 10 hours with free_peak_oref produces a long tail, and the largest falls occur at 240 to 360 minutes rather than 120 minutes, yet a longer DIA is conservative by design because more insulin on board is counted, so DIA is characterized as an amplifier of evening carry-over rather than a cause. Evening corrections at 21:51 to 22:30 local reached their trough at 180 to 240 minutes and were still suppressing at 360 minutes, placing residual insulin on board into the 01:00 local hour that carries 18.5 percent below range.

The ISF row cannot be judged independently of the Dynamic ISF group.

The sign convention of the Dynamic ISF adjustment factor in this build is unconfirmed. Custom modifiers such as UAM Boost, prTrial, twin and antBackout are undocumented and unquantified.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and are the only mechanism responding to meals, because carbohydrates are never announced. Activation conditions are internally consistent: smb_always_enabled true makes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false effectively dormant, and both are doubly dormant with zero carbohydrate entries. One material behavior is confirmed: smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, so the 135 mg/dL temporary targets of 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18 created afternoon SMB blackouts. The window starting 08-17 at 13:30 local rose from 126 to 190 mg/dL at 180 minutes and then fell to 111 and 95 mg/dL once SMB resumed, which validates the mechanism and requires those two afternoons to be excluded from parameter inference. The configured SMB caps are not binding in this build. Expressed in minutes of profile basal, 15 minutes yields about 0.125 U at the 16:00 basal of 0.5 U per hour and 20 minutes yields about 0.167 U, yet observed doses exceed those ceilings: on 08-07 the reason states standardMaxBolus 0.2 while microbolusing 0.4 U, and on 08-19 at 16:54 local a UAM High Boost delivered an SMB of 1.6 U at 264 mg/dL with insulin on board already 4.73 U. Custom boost logic therefore overrides the inventory caps, so reducing those caps would produce little real restraint. The 3-minute interval permits frequent redosing and contributes to accumulation but remains a secondary lever behind the sensitivity curve.

analysis_steps.findings: The sensitivity configuration is internally coherent: Autosens disabled, Autosens target adjustment disabled in both directions, Dynamic ISF enabled at 70 percent, oref1 sensitivity algorithm. Observed sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and 1.00 are read as neutral or mildly reduced current adjustments produced by the dynamic path, not as evidence that Autosens is disabled in effect and not as duplicate counting, and no evidence of two stacked sensitivity engines was found. The material finding is the shape of the effective sensitivity curve: weak in the sustained afternoon band and strong above roughly 200 mg/dL, which is a self-consistent mechanism for 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 followed by 15.3 percent below range at 19:00. On safety limits, max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is 15 times the largest profile basal of 0.8 and never binds, because the real ceiling in the logs is a maximum safe basal of 4 U per hour produced by the safety multipliers. max_iob_units of 25 is roughly 1.5 times the entire daily profile basal and provides no practical brake, while observed insulin on board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U with carbohydrates on board 0. At the 27.8 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity recorded at that moment, 5.935 U represents a very large pending fall with no declared counterbalancing carbohydrate and a 10-hour DIA to unwind it. The carbohydrate absorption model is dormant, because min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 act on carbohydrates on board, which is 0 throughout.

The maximum insulin on board component is the only lever here that is independent of profile rows, while the Dynamic ISF factor is dependent on the ISF row and on profile basal, so the two must not be changed in the same step.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The sign convention of dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent in this build is unconfirmed, so no numeric replacement can be responsibly proposed. The source of effective targets below the profile floor, including 80 mg/dL, is unidentified and lies outside decision_inventory. Three GLP-1 doses within seven days make sensitivity non-stationary, so all conclusions here are period averages.

analysis_steps.findings: The user declaration block aaps_profile.analysis_context exists and is authored, with source declared_by_user and declared_at 2026-08-21T21:08:10Z, but meal_strategies is an empty array, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. No prebolus_minutes, immediate_bolus_percent or e-carb fields are present to reproduce, and because strategy_stable_for_period is null no representative period declaration can be asserted. Observed execution is entirely reactive: all 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses, 655 insulin entries total 275.95 U at about 19.7 U per day against a 16.2 U per day profile basal, and no bolus is linked to a carbohydrate entry. Prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage are therefore mechanically undefined, because no announced carbohydrate exists to precede or to split. Full six-hour review shows a recurring signature: of nine windows starting at or above 160 mg/dL, six fell below 95 mg/dL and four below 60 mg/dL within six hours, including 172 to 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-13, 234 to 41 and 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-14, 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-16 and 264 to 88 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-19. Of twelve windows starting below 160 mg/dL, nine reached 88 mg/dL or lower, which shows the downward drift is not solely a high-glucose artifact and supports an evening basal and insulin on board carry-over contribution. Rebound rises too fast to be endogenous were observed, including 47 to 204 mg/dL in two hours on 08-13 and 71 to 225 mg/dL in one hour on 08-12, indicating that glucose-raising intake occurs and is invisible to the algorithm; no claim is made about composition. Bolus stacking is visible, for example 0.2 U at 16:20 followed by 1.1 U at 16:30 on 08-14 preceding the 56 mg/dL reading at 120 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbohydrate entries are absent. extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is empty and all 24 therapy response windows carry is_extended_carbs false. E-carb amount, start offset, duration and observed action time therefore cannot be assessed, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate average, because the average field is null and no meal-linked evidence exists. E-carbs are treated strictly as the AAPS carbohydrate announcement construct that feeds carbohydrates on board and the absorption model, not as a pump extended or dual-wave bolus; neither construct is evidenced here and the absence of one does not substitute for the other. The only absorption-like signal is the unlogged rebound behavior of roughly 50 to 155 mg/dL per hour, which is characteristic of rapid rather than extended absorption and gives no support for introducing extended carbohydrate entry now. min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7 remain dormant with carbohydrates on board 0 throughout. Forward-looking consistency caveat only: if announcement begins, a 7-hour maximum absorption combined with a 10-hour DIA would create long overlapping carbohydrate and insulin tails.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory produced four corrections to earlier reasoning. First, the inventory contains exactly 23 items, 17 profile and 6 AAPS, and every AAPS component has a non-null current_value, so verify is unavailable for all six AAPS groups and each must resolve to change or keep. Second, the apparent basal shape mismatch is downgraded: with meals unannounced, temp basals of 0 to 4 U per hour overriding the profile continuously, and SMB caps scaling with profile basal, no basal row can be separated from meal and automation effects, so all seven basal rows are kept. Third, DIA is downgraded from candidate cause to amplifier, because a longer DIA counts more insulin on board and is conservative by design, and the magnitude of the falls is explained by dose size at the peak rather than by the decay model. Fourth, the ISF row itself cannot be changed responsibly, because 56 mg/dL per unit functions only as a base for Dynamic ISF and the effective value never equals it, so moving the base would also move the protective high sensitivity of 108 to 124 mg/dL per unit that applies below 95 mg/dL. Ranking for the dominant pattern of afternoon hyperglycemia followed by evening hypoglycemia: the Dynamic ISF curve shape and late UAM detection due to non-announcement are the two well-supported and complementary primary drivers; evening insulin on board carry-over under a 10-hour DIA is a supported secondary contributor for 19:00 to 03:00; basal shape remains plausible but confounded; sub-profile effective targets remain unresolved and block any target change. The conservative sequence is therefore one independent hard guardrail that does not alter the shape of normal dosing, then making meals visible so that carb ratio, prebolus and absorption become measurable, and only then addressing the sensitivity curve one parameter at a time.

The maximum insulin on board component is the only lever independent of profile rows and of the Dynamic ISF curve, which is why it is sequenced first. Carbohydrate announcement is observation-enabling rather than an insulin-delivery change, which is why it can follow without breaching the one-change-at-a-time rule.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unresolved and still blocking: the source of effective targets below the profile floor including 80 mg/dL, the sign convention of the Dynamic ISF adjustment factor in this build, the magnitude of the custom boost multipliers, the basal versus bolus split of total daily dose, and the non-stationarity introduced by three GLP-1 doses within seven days.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and is not a limiting factor for any inference: 98.7 percent coverage, stable 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, zero invalid and zero duplicate entries, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes.
Overall control is good by consensus metrics: time in range 86.0 percent, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL and coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, which is below the 36 percent variability threshold.
The overnight fasting-like window from 02:00 to 07:00 local is stable, with hourly means of 99.5 to 106.0 mg/dL, time in range of 89.2 to 98.7 percent and negligible time above range.
Local hours 08:00 and 09:00 record 0.0 percent time below range and 07:00 records 1.3 percent, making the morning the safest window in the dataset for any future observation or trial.

The profile is complete and internally consistent: all basal, carb ratio, ISF, target and DIA fields are populated, and the basal total of 16.2 U per day matches the profile switch note describing 16.2 U per day with a flat ISF.
Two automation limits are already more conservative than common defaults: max_smb_basal_minutes at 15 and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes at 20 against the usual 30 minutes.
Record keeping is strong, with documented site changes, sensor changes, GLP-1 doses, temporary targets and a profile switch, which materially improves the interpretability of the period.
issues: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the 4 percent goal and is concentrated in two clock windows: 18.5 percent at 01:00 local and 15.3 percent at 19:00 local, with 00:00, 02:00, 03:00 and 23:00 all near 10 percent.
Level 2 hypoglycemia occurred on three days, with 42 mg/dL on 08-13, 41 mg/dL on 08-14 and 42 mg/dL on 08-21, and 8 of 14 days reached a minimum at or below 55 mg/dL.

Insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 08-19 and 5.935 U on 08-21 with carbohydrates on board 0, the latter at 245 mg/dL with an effective sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit and a further 2.12 U requested at a 4 U per hour temp rate.
The configured maximum insulin on board of 25 U is roughly 1.5 times the entire daily profile basal of 16.2 U and never engaged during the period, so it provides no practical brake on accumulation.

The effective sensitivity curve is weak through the sustained afternoon band and strong above 200 mg/dL, ranging from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile base of 56 and crossing it near 170 to 190 mg/dL, which matches the observed sequence of 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 followed by 15.3 percent below range at 19:00.

Corrections started above 160 mg/dL are frequently followed by a low: of nine such windows, six fell below 95 mg/dL and four below 60 mg/dL within six hours, including 172 to 47 mg/dL on 08-13 and 234 to 41 mg/dL on 08-14.

No carbohydrates were announced in 14 days, so UAM is the sole meal response and always acts after the rise, while rebound rises of 50 to 155 mg/dL per hour show that glucose-raising intake occurs and is invisible to the algorithm.
All five carb ratio segments are unfalsifiable in this period, because carbohydrate entries are 0 and carbohydrates on board are 0 in every sampled loop status.

Configured SMB caps are overridden by custom boost logic: the 20-minute UAM allowance corresponds to about 0.167 U at the 16:00 basal of 0.5 U per hour, yet 1.6 U was delivered on 08-19, and on 08-07 the reason string states standardMaxBolus 0.2 while microbolusing 0.4 U.

Effective loop targets of 80 mg/dL appear on the most aggressive high-glucose loops on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21, below the profile floor of 90 mg/dL, from a source that is not Autosens because target adjustment is disabled in both directions.

High temporary targets create multi-hour SMB blackouts, because smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false: on 08-17 glucose rose from 126 to 190 mg/dL across the 180-minute temporary target and then fell to 111 and 95 mg/dL once SMB resumed.
The period is non-stationary, containing three GLP-1 1.25 mg doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20, an occlusion with pump error on 08-19, three site changes, two sensor changes and one profile switch.

The profile lists 13.0 g per unit for the 00:00 to 04:00 carb ratio while loop output repeatedly reports 13.3 g per unit, a difference of about 2 percent that suggests the running configuration may not be identical to the reviewed profile.

recommendations.title: Reduce the maximum insulin on board ceiling as a single independent safety guardrail
recommendations.description: This is the primary recommendation, because it is the only identified lever that is independent of every profile row and of the Dynamic ISF curve, so it can be discussed alone without breaching the one-change-at-a-time principle. The configured value of 25 U is roughly 1.5 times the entire daily profile basal of 16.2 U and never engaged. Observed insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 08-19 at 16:54 local and 5.935 U on 08-21 at 22:09 local, both with carbohydrates on board 0, and at the 27.8 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity recorded in the second case that quantity represents a very large pending fall with a 10-hour DIA to unwind it. Four of nine correction windows starting above 160 mg/dL fell below 60 mg/dL within six hours. A ceiling near 8 U would sit above all routine operation while capping the two extreme accumulation episodes. The exact value is for the user and care team to determine. This limits the consequence rather than the cause, which is why it is paired with the observation steps below.

suggested_change.rationale: Backstop against observed accumulation to 5.935 U with zero carbohydrates on board and a 27.8 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity
suggested_change.independent_of: All profile rows and the Dynamic ISF adjustment factor
suggested_change.observation_window: 14 days, tracking whether the ceiling engages and whether time below range in the 18:00 to 03:00 local window falls from the current 7.7, 15.3, 11.4 and 18.5 percent hourly values

recommendations.title: Announce one recurring meal so that carb ratio and meal timing become measurable
recommendations.description: This is observation-enabling rather than an insulin-delivery change, so it can run alongside the guardrail without breaching the sequencing rule. With zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days and carbohydrates on board 0 in every status, carb ratio, prebolus lead time, immediate bolus percentage and the absorption model are all unfalsifiable, while rebound rises of 50 to 155 mg/dL per hour prove that intake occurs unrecorded. Announcing the morning meal for 7 to 10 consecutive days with an approximate carbohydrate amount entered at the first bite would create the first paired carbohydrate, insulin and response data of the period. The morning is proposed because 08:00 and 09:00 local record 0.0 percent time below range and 07:00 records 1.3 percent.

suggested_change.to: One recurring morning meal announced daily for 7 to 10 days with approximate grams and first-bite time
suggested_change.rationale: Creates carbohydrates on board so that carb ratio, prebolus timing and absorption become measurable, and gives UAM a head start instead of sole responsibility
suggested_change.observation_window: 7 to 10 days before any further parameter change

recommendations.title: Confirm the Dynamic ISF factor convention before considering any sensitivity change
recommendations.description: The effective sensitivity curve is the best-supported mechanism for afternoon hyperglycemia followed by evening hypoglycemia, reaching 27.8 to 37.9 mg/dL per unit above 200 mg/dL against a profile base of 56. The review direction would be to make high-glucose corrections less aggressive without flattening the protective 108 to 124 mg/dL per unit that applies below 95 mg/dL. No numeric replacement is proposed, because the sign convention of dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent differs between builds and this branch contains undocumented boost logic, so an unverified number could increase aggressiveness instead of reducing it. This change is dependent on the ISF row and on profile basal and must not be made in the same step as the maximum insulin on board change or the meal announcement.

suggested_change.direction: confirm the build convention first, then reduce dosing aggressiveness above 200 mg/dL
suggested_change.to: Not proposed until build documentation confirms which direction weakens high-glucose dosing
suggested_change.sequence_position: Third, only after the guardrail and the announcement have each been observed separately

recommendations.title: Identify the source of effective targets below the profile floor before any target change
recommendations.description: Profile targets are 90, 100 from 08:00 and 90 from 23:00 mg/dL, yet loop output shows effective targets of 80 mg/dL on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21, precisely on the loops that dose most heavily. Autosens target adjustment is disabled in both directions, so Autosens is not the source. A target below the profile floor applied when dosing is most aggressive is a material safety consideration, and it blocks any responsible target change in either direction until the origin is located in the build settings. This is why all three target rows are kept unchanged in this review.

suggested_change.to: Identify which build setting or override produces the observed 80 mg/dL effective target
suggested_change.blocking: All target row decisions until resolved

recommendations.title: Hold all basal segments despite the apparent shape mismatch
recommendations.description: The lowest basal of 0.5 U per hour from 16:00 sits under the highest glucose hours and the highest evening basal of 0.7 U per hour from 19:00 sits over the worst evening hypoglycemia hour, which superficially suggests a shape problem. Three factors block action. Meals are entirely unannounced, so the afternoon plateau cannot be separated from post-meal excursions. Temp basals of 0 to 4 U per hour override the profile continuously. Most importantly, SMB caps are expressed in minutes of profile basal, so raising the 16:00 segment from 0.5 to 0.7 U per hour would also raise the UAM SMB ceiling from about 0.167 to 0.233 U and lift the current-basal safety ceiling, making automation more aggressive going into the 18:00 and 19:00 hours that already carry 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range.

suggested_change.rationale: Coupling between profile basal and SMB caps means a basal-only change is not actually isolated
suggested_change.revisit_after: The maximum insulin on board guardrail has been observed for 14 days and 7 to 10 days of announced meals exist, starting with the 19:00 segment

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows unchanged, including all seven basal segments, the flat ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, the five carb ratios, the three targets and the 10-hour DIA. Place the concrete action outside the profile for now: lower the maximum insulin on board ceiling as a single independent automation guardrail and begin announcing one recurring morning meal, then verify the evening basal question with the precise check below.
profile_recommendation.rationale: No profile row is separable from automation and meal effects with the current data. The seven basal rows are confounded because meals are never announced, because temp basals of 0 to 4 U per hour override the profile continuously, and because SMB caps are expressed in minutes of profile basal, so a basal change would simultaneously change automation aggressiveness in the same hour. The five carb ratios are unfalsifiable with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0 and carbohydrates on board 0 in every sampled status. The flat ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit is never used directly, because Dynamic ISF produced effective values from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, so changing the base would also move the protective high sensitivity that applies below 95 mg/dL and would work against the primary problem of 5.1 percent time below range. The three targets are blocked because effective targets of 80 mg/dL appear below the profile floor from an unidentified source while Autosens target adjustment is disabled. DIA of 10 hours is conservative by design, since a longer duration counts more insulin on board, so shortening it would increase dosing in exactly the wrong direction.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After the maximum insulin on board ceiling has been lowered and left as the only change for 14 days, compare hourly time below range for the evening and overnight block against the current baseline of 7.7 percent at 18:00, 15.3 percent at 19:00, 11.4 percent at 00:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00 local, and record the peak insulin on board each day together with the variable sensitivity value at that moment. If the 19:00 hour still exceeds roughly 8 percent time below range while peak insulin on board is now capped, the 0.7 U per hour segment starting at 19:00 becomes the single next profile row to examine, before any other basal segment and before any target or ISF row.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence is mixed rather than absent. Local hour 00:00 shows 11.4 percent and 01:00 shows 18.5 percent time below range, which superficially suggests excess. Against this, mean glucose rises from 90.6 at 01:00 to 106.0 at 04:00 while time below range falls to 3.0 percent, a pattern that fits decaying evening insulin on board under a 10-hour DIA rather than an excessive overnight rate. Uncertainty: evening corrections at 21:51 to 22:30 local were still suppressing glucose at 360 minutes, so carry-over cannot be separated from the basal rate. Dependencies: the maximum insulin on board guardrail and the Dynamic ISF curve both act on this window and are sequenced ahead of any basal change.

Evidence supports no change: local hour 05:00 shows a mean of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range, 0.0 percent above and 4.8 percent below. Uncertainty: this hour is also the tail of the overnight insulin on board carry-over, so its apparent adequacy is partly a product of upstream events rather than proof that the rate is correct. Dependencies: none that would justify acting here before the guardrail and the meal announcement steps.

Evidence: local hours 06:00 and 07:00 show means of 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 and 98.7 percent time in range and near-zero time above range, so the early part of the highest basal segment performs well. The rise to 132.9 at 09:00 and 148.0 at 10:00 begins inside this segment, but with zero carbohydrate entries a morning meal is at least as plausible as a basal deficit. Uncertainty: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 preceded a sensor change by two hours, so an artifact cannot be excluded. Dependencies: this segment sets the most permissive SMB caps of the day, about 0.20 and 0.267 U, so raising it would also increase automation aggressiveness.

Evidence: this segment spans hourly means of 132.3 to 162.8 mg/dL with 7.5 to 32.1 percent time above range, which would superficially argue for an increase. The change is withheld because meals are entirely unannounced and carbohydrates on board are 0 throughout, so the elevation cannot be separated from post-meal excursions handled late by UAM. Uncertainty: the afternoons of 08-17 and 08-18 inside this segment contained 180-minute SMB blackouts from 135 mg/dL temporary targets and are excluded from inference. Dependencies: any increase would also raise the SMB caps and the current-basal safety ceiling feeding into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia window.

Evidence: this is the strongest apparent mismatch, since the lowest basal of the day sits under 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and 148.9 mg/dL at 17:00 with 22.6 percent above range. The change is withheld for a mechanical reason: SMB caps are expressed in minutes of profile basal, so raising this segment to 0.7 U per hour would lift the UAM SMB ceiling from about 0.167 to 0.233 U and raise the current-basal safety ceiling, increasing aggressiveness immediately before the 18:00 and 19:00 hours that already carry 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range. Uncertainty: unannounced afternoon meals remain a fully plausible alternative explanation. Dependencies: this row cannot be isolated from aaps.core.smb_delivery or from the Dynamic ISF curve.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL on the steep descent from the afternoon peak, and the lows follow boosted corrections rather than a steady basal excess, for example the 08-14 window falling from 234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes after 1.3 U was delivered within 10 minutes. Uncertainty: a basal contribution cannot be excluded, only deprioritized. Dependencies: the Dynamic ISF curve and the maximum insulin on board ceiling both act on this descent and are sequenced first.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 carries the second highest time below range of the period at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the highest evening basal begins exactly here, so this is a genuine candidate. The change is withheld because the same hour follows the afternoon peak and its boosted corrections, and because four of four evening correction windows drifted low with no preceding rise, implicating insulin on board carry-over under a 10-hour DIA alongside the basal rate. Uncertainty: basal and carry-over cannot be separated with the current data. Dependencies: this is the highest-priority basal row to revisit once the maximum insulin on board ceiling has been observed for 14 days, and it should be examined before any other basal segment.

Evidence: unfalsifiable in this period, because carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board are 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, so no bolus-to-carbohydrate outcome exists for this segment. Uncertainty: loop reason strings repeatedly report 13.3 g per unit in this window against the profile value of 13.0, about 2 percent, which suggests the running configuration may differ from the reviewed profile and is worth confirming, though it is not itself a reason to change the value. Dependencies: becomes assessable only after carbohydrate announcement begins.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, because zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board 0 mean no meal response can be attributed to this segment. The value is confirmed consistent between profile and loop output, which reports 11.1 in this window. Uncertainty: no outcome data at all exists for this ratio. Dependencies: requires the meal announcement step before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, despite this segment covering the most reproducible excursion in the dataset, the rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local. With no carbohydrate entered there is no calculated bolus and no measurable ratio, and the value matches loop output of 13.2. Uncertainty: nothing resolvable from this package. Dependencies: this is the segment that the proposed morning meal announcement would make measurable first, and it should be the first carb ratio examined once 7 to 10 days of paired data exist.

Evidence: unfalsifiable. This is the strongest carb ratio of the day and covers the highest-glucose hours, but with zero carbohydrate entries there is no way to test it. The value matches loop output of 10.5. Uncertainty: the elevation in this window is confounded by unannounced meals, by the 180-minute SMB blackouts on 08-17 and 08-18, and by the Dynamic ISF curve being weakest in exactly this glucose band. Dependencies: assessment requires both meal announcement and resolution of the sensitivity question.

Evidence: unfalsifiable, because zero carbohydrate entries and carbohydrates on board 0 mean no evening meal response can be attributed here. The value matches loop output of 12.6. Uncertainty: the evening window shows a distinct downward drift, with four of four correction windows falling and no preceding rise, but that is a basal, DIA and insulin on board pattern and must not be attributed to a carb ratio. Dependencies: requires meal announcement before assessment.

Evidence: the static value is never used directly for dosing. With Dynamic ISF enabled at a 70 percent factor and Autosens disabled, observed effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit, crossing 56 only near 170 to 190 mg/dL, with 124 at 70 mg/dL, 108 at 84, 71 to 87 at 120 to 140 and 27.8 to 37.9 at 245 to 262. Changing the base would shift the whole curve, including the protective high sensitivity at low glucose, which would work against the primary problem of 5.1 percent time below range. Uncertainty: whether the curve shape or the base is at fault cannot be separated without knowing this build sign convention. Dependencies: inseparable from aaps.core.sensitivity, and only one of the two may be touched, with the automation group being the correct target.

Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 carry 10.1 to 18.5 percent time below range, which would ordinarily argue for raising the overnight target. The change is blocked because the effective target used by the loop is not derivable from this row: observed values include 80, 84, 86, 87, 96.4 and 97 mg/dL, and 80 appears on the most aggressive high-glucose loops, below the profile floor, while Autosens target adjustment is disabled in both directions. Uncertainty: raising a row that is being overridden by an unidentified mechanism could produce no effect or an unpredictable one. Dependencies: blocked until the source of the sub-profile target is identified.

Evidence: this daytime target covers the safest window in the dataset, with 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00 local, so there is no hypoglycemia argument for raising it, and the afternoon time above range is better explained by the sensitivity curve and unannounced meals than by the target. Uncertainty: the same override problem applies, with effective targets of 80 mg/dL observed on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21 within this segment. Dependencies: blocked until the source of the sub-profile target is identified.

Evidence: local hour 23:00 shows 10.1 percent time below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL, so a higher late-evening target is a plausible future direction. The change is withheld for the same override reason as the other target rows, and because the evening lows are better attributed to insulin on board carry-over from corrections at 21:51 to 22:30 local that were still suppressing glucose at 360 minutes. Uncertainty: target, basal and carry-over all act on the same hours and are not separated. Dependencies: blocked until the sub-profile target source is identified and until the maximum insulin on board guardrail has been observed.

Evidence: DIA of 10 hours with free_peak_oref produces a long tail, and the largest observed falls occur at 240 to 360 minutes rather than 120 minutes, which initially suggested DIA as a candidate. That reasoning is corrected here, because a longer DIA is conservative by design, counting more insulin on board at dosing time, so shortening it would make the algorithm dose more, which is the wrong direction against 5.1 percent time below range. The magnitude of the falls is explained by dose size at the peak under an effective sensitivity of 27.8 to 37.9 mg/dL per unit above 200 mg/dL. Uncertainty: the insulin peak time is not exposed, so the modeled tail shape cannot be verified. Dependencies: DIA amplifies the evening carry-over in the 19:00 to 03:00 window and should be revisited only after the sensitivity and basal questions are settled.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable and the decision is keep. Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, UAM is the only mechanism responding to meals, and disabling it would remove the sole meal response and would predictably worsen the 14.0 to 32.1 percent time above range in the 12:00 to 17:00 local band; 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U were delivered with carbohydrates on board 0 throughout. The two components are mutually consistent and consistent with smb_always_enabled true. Uncertainty: none material for this group. Dependencies: the problem lies in dose size, governed by aaps.core.sensitivity and the custom boost logic, not in enablement.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: the set is internally consistent, since smb_always_enabled true makes the carbohydrates on board and after-carbs conditions dormant, and they are doubly dormant with zero carbohydrate entries. One material behavior is documented rather than changed: with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the 135 mg/dL temporary targets of 180 minutes on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed SMB entirely, and on 08-17 glucose rose from 126 to 190 mg/dL across that interval before falling to 111 and 95 mg/dL when SMB resumed. Uncertainty: the intent behind each temporary target is unknown, and the user appears to be using high targets deliberately as a manual brake. Dependencies: removing that brake while the sensitivity curve is unresolved would increase risk, so revisit only after the sensitivity question is settled.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: All three components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: the two basal-minute caps are already below the common 30-minute defaults and are demonstrably not binding, since the 20-minute UAM allowance corresponds to about 0.167 U at the 16:00 basal of 0.5 U per hour yet a UAM High Boost delivered 1.6 U on 08-19 at 264 mg/dL, and on 08-07 the reason string states standardMaxBolus 0.2 while microbolusing 0.4 U. Lowering caps that are already overridden would create the appearance of restraint without the substance. Uncertainty: the magnitude of the custom boost multipliers is unquantified and outside decision_inventory, so the true ceiling on a single SMB cannot be derived. Dependencies: these caps scale with profile basal, so they are coupled to every basal row, and the 3-minute interval is retained as a secondary candidate only if the sensitivity lever is declined, never changed alongside the maximum insulin on board ceiling.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable, and change applies to the max_iob_units component only while max_basal_u_per_hour is kept. Evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is 15 times the largest profile basal of 0.8 and never binds, because the real ceiling in the logs is a maximum safe basal of 4 U per hour produced by the safety multipliers, so lowering 12 would be inert until it fell below 4, at which point it would become a dependent change. max_iob_units of 25 is roughly 1.5 times the entire daily profile basal of 16.2 U and never engaged, while observed insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 08-19 and 5.935 U on 08-21, both with carbohydrates on board 0, the latter at an effective sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit with a further 2.12 U requested, and four of nine correction windows starting above 160 mg/dL fell below 60 mg/dL within six hours. A ceiling of 8 U sits above all routine operation while capping the two extreme accumulation episodes. Uncertainty: the exact value depends on the basal versus bolus split of total daily dose, which cannot be computed from the 40 sampled treatments, so 8 U is a supported starting point for discussion rather than a derived optimum. Dependencies: this is the only lever independent of all profile rows and of the Dynamic ISF curve, which is why it is sequenced first and alone.

All five components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable and the decision must be change or keep. Evidence: this group contains the best-supported mechanism in the analysis, since the effective sensitivity curve is weak through the sustained 130 to 163 mg/dL afternoon band and strong above 200 mg/dL, crossing the static profile ISF near 170 to 190 mg/dL, matching 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 followed by 15.3 percent below range at 19:00. Keep is nonetheless correct now for two reasons: the sign convention of dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent differs between builds and this branch contains undocumented boost logic, so change may not be used without a supported value, and this group is dependent on the profile ISF row and on profile basal so it cannot be changed in the same step as the maximum insulin on board ceiling. Interpretation note: sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.00 are read as neutral or mildly reduced current adjustments from the dynamic path, not as a disabled Autosens and not as duplicate counting. Uncertainty: three GLP-1 doses within seven days make the period non-stationary. Dependencies: sequenced third, after the guardrail and the meal announcement have each been observed separately.

Both components have non-null values, so verify is unavailable. Evidence: both settings act on carbohydrates on board, which is 0 in every sampled loop status, with zero carbohydrate entries and zero extended carbohydrate entries in 14 days, so they are entirely dormant and nothing in this package can support a change in either direction; min_5m_carbimpact of 8 is also the common default. Uncertainty: none resolvable while the settings are dormant, and no duration is inferred from average_extended_carb_duration_min because it is null. Dependencies: a forward-looking caveat is recorded that a 7-hour maximum absorption combined with a 10-hour DIA would create long overlapping carbohydrate and insulin tails once announcement begins, which becomes assessable only after 7 to 10 days of announced meals produce a real absorption curve.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Because no carbohydrates are announced, there is presently no meal strategy to tune, only a reactive UAM strategy that detects meals late and then over-corrects. Keep SMB and UAM enabled, since they are the only meal response present. Do not adopt any prebolus lead time and do not adopt an immediate bolus percentage from this package, because the user declaration contains no meal strategy entries and telemetry contains no announced carbohydrate, so neither value can be derived and neither should be invented. Do not introduce e-carbs yet, because the observed unlogged rises of roughly 50 to 155 mg/dL per hour are rapid rather than extended, so standard carbohydrate entry is the appropriate first construct, and e-carbs are in any case a carbohydrate announcement mechanism feeding carbohydrates on board rather than a pump extended bolus. The single useful step is to make meals visible by announcing one recurring meal with an approximate carbohydrate amount entered at the first bite, which creates carbohydrates on board for the first time, gives UAM a head start instead of sole responsibility, and makes carb ratio, prebolus timing and the absorption model measurable.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: All 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false; carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty, extended_carb_entries is 0 and average_extended_carb_duration_min is null; carbohydrates on board are 0 in every sampled loop status. About 19.7 U per day of correction and UAM insulin is delivered against a 16.2 U per day profile basal. Of nine windows starting at or above 160 mg/dL, six fell below 95 mg/dL and four below 60 mg/dL within six hours, while rebound rises such as 47 to 204 mg/dL in two hours on 08-13 and 71 to 225 mg/dL in one hour on 08-12 show that glucose-raising intake occurs and is invisible to the algorithm. The declaration block exists and is authored, with meal_strategies as an empty array and strategy_stable_for_period null, so no declared value is contradicted by telemetry; the situation is simply that no declared meal parameters exist to compare against observed execution, which is why confidence is low rather than why data are called missing.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log the morning meal for 7 to 10 consecutive days by recording the approximate carbohydrate amount and the clock time of the first bite, and enter those carbohydrates in AAPS at that time. This single observation makes carb ratio falsifiable for the first time, establishes whether a prebolus lead time is needed and how long, and produces the first real absorption curve against which min_5m_carbimpact, meal_max_absorption_hours and the e-carb question can be judged. The morning is proposed because local hours 08:00 and 09:00 record 0.0 percent time below range and 07:00 records 1.3 percent, the lowest hypoglycemia risk of any window in the period.

exceptions.suggestion: If meal announcement is trialled in only one window, trial it here first.
exceptions.rationale: This is the largest and most reproducible recurring rise, with hourly means moving from 99.5 at 07:00 to 110.5 at 08:00, 132.9 at 09:00 and 148.0 at 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, and individual windows rising from 100 to 188 mg/dL in 60 minutes on 08-14 and 164 to 205 mg/dL in 60 minutes on 08-19. It is also the safest window, with 0.0 percent time below range at 08:00 and 09:00, and it carries the highest profile basal of 0.8 U per hour so the basal-minute SMB caps are at their most permissive and UAM behavior is least distorted.

exceptions.pattern: Late evening declines, approximately 21:00 to 03:00 local
exceptions.suggestion: Treat this window as outside meal strategy entirely and do not address it with meal timing or bolus percentage changes.
exceptions.rationale: Four of four evening correction windows drifted steadily low with no preceding rise, reaching 74 mg/dL at 120 minutes, 69 at 180 to 240 minutes, 82 to 83 at 180 to 240 minutes and 57 at 240 minutes, and the pattern continues into the 00:00 to 03:00 local band with 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent time below range. There is no meal signature here; with a 10-hour DIA the evening correction insulin on board persists into the 01:00 hour while profile basal is at its highest evening value of 0.7 U per hour. A meal-strategy change here would mis-target the cause and could mask the basal, DIA and insulin on board question that remains open.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before changing anything: confirm with the care team that the reviewed profile matches the profile actually running, paying particular attention to the 00:00 to 04:00 carb ratio, which the profile lists as 13.0 g per unit while loop output repeatedly reports 13.3 g per unit. Also confirm the pump and reservoir setup implied by the note describing dilute U200 basal, because insulin concentration affects how every unit value in this review should be read.

Step 1, first and alone: discuss lowering max_iob_units from 25 U to about 8 U as a single independent guardrail, changing nothing else at the same time. This does not alter the shape of routine dosing; it caps the tail risk seen at 4.73 U and 5.935 U while the underlying cause is still being separated. Observe for 14 days.

Step 2, observation during Step 1: each day record the peak insulin on board reached, the variable sensitivity value at that moment, and time below range for the 18:00 to 03:00 local window, comparing against the current baselines of 7.7 percent at 18:00, 15.3 percent at 19:00, 11.4 percent at 00:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00.

Step 3, in parallel because it is observation-enabling rather than an insulin-delivery change: begin announcing the morning meal for 7 to 10 consecutive days, entering an approximate carbohydrate amount at the time of the first bite. Do not introduce e-carbs, and do not adopt a prebolus lead time or an immediate bolus percentage yet, because the purpose of this step is to generate the data that would make those answerable.

Step 4, investigation with no setting change: identify which build setting or override produces the effective targets of 80 mg/dL observed on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21, given a profile floor of 90 mg/dL and Autosens target adjustment disabled in both directions. No target row should be changed until this is resolved.

Step 5, investigation with no setting change: confirm from this specific build documentation which direction of dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent weakens high-glucose dosing, because the sign convention differs between builds and this branch contains additional undocumented boost logic.

Step 6, only after Steps 1 to 5 and only if lows persist: with the convention confirmed, discuss adjusting the Dynamic ISF factor so that effective sensitivity above 200 mg/dL moves toward the profile value of 56 mg/dL per unit, without flattening the protective 108 to 124 mg/dL per unit that currently applies below 95 mg/dL. Change this alone and observe for 14 days.

Step 7, only if lows in the 19:00 to 03:00 local window persist after Steps 1 and 6: revisit the 19:00 basal segment of 0.7 U per hour as the single highest-priority basal row, before any other basal segment, recognising that this row also scales the UAM SMB cap in that window.

Step 8, only after 7 to 10 days of announced meals exist: reassess the 08:00 carb ratio of 13.2 g per unit first, then prebolus timing and immediate bolus percentage, and only then whether the absorption settings of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and 7 hours fit the observed curve, noting the overlap between a 7-hour absorption window and a 10-hour DIA.

Throughout: make one change at a time, allow at least 14 days of observation between insulin-delivery changes, and repeat the review after any further GLP-1 dose change, because three doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 fall inside this period and make the underlying sensitivity non-stationary.
education: Dynamic ISF means the sensitivity used for dosing is calculated from current glucose and total daily dose rather than taken directly from the profile. That is why the flat profile value of 56 mg/dL per unit never appears in loop output, and why the effective value ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit across this period. Reviewing the static profile number in isolation can therefore be misleading in this configuration.

Maximum SMB size is configured in minutes of profile basal rather than in units. A 20-minute UAM allowance corresponds to about 0.167 U when basal is 0.5 U per hour but about 0.267 U when basal is 0.8 U per hour, so the profile basal value quietly controls how aggressive the automation can be at each hour and a basal change is rarely an isolated change.

A longer duration of insulin action makes the algorithm more conservative, not less, because more insulin on board is counted when the next dose is calculated. Shortening DIA to address lows usually has the opposite of the intended effect.

Time below range is best interpreted by clock hour rather than as a single daily figure. A period average of 5.1 percent conceals hours at 18.5 and 15.3 percent alongside hours at 0.0 percent, and where the lows sit relative to the daily peaks is what distinguishes an overshoot from a steady insulin excess.

When carbohydrates are never entered, the algorithm can only react after glucose has already risen. Announcing carbohydrates does not merely change one dose; it creates carbohydrates on board, which changes how the algorithm predicts, how it constrains microboluses, and whether carb ratio can ever be evaluated from outcome data.

E-carbs in AAPS are a way of announcing carbohydrate with a start offset and a duration so that it feeds the carbohydrates-on-board model. They are not the same as a pump extended or dual-wave bolus, which delivers insulin over time. The two behave differently and should not be substituted for one another.

A sensitivity ratio of 1 in loop output means the current adjustment is neutral, not that a sensitivity feature is switched off. Reading it as disabled would misattribute behavior that is actually being produced by the active dynamic sensitivity path.

GLP-1 medication can change insulin sensitivity and gastric emptying. With three doses inside a 14-day review window, any sensitivity conclusion drawn from that window is a period average rather than a stable estimate, and patterns may shift as dosing settles.

A safety limit such as maximum insulin on board behaves differently from a tuning parameter. It does not change the shape of routine dosing; it caps the worst case, which is why it can often be adjusted independently while more entangled parameters are still being investigated.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice, and no setting has been or will be changed automatically. Every proposal here must be independently verified with the treating clinician or diabetes team before anything is altered.

Make only one change at a time and allow enough observation between changes, generally around 14 days for insulin-delivery settings, so that each effect can be attributed. Several parameters here are coupled, notably profile basal with SMB caps and profile ISF with Dynamic ISF, so simultaneous changes would make the result uninterpretable.

Hypoglycemia is the leading finding of this review, with 5.1 percent time below range, readings of 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-21, and 8 of 14 days reaching a minimum at or below 55 mg/dL. Monitor glucose closely during any change and keep fast-acting carbohydrate available, particularly in the 18:00 to 03:00 local window.

No proposal in this review increases insulin delivery in any window. The apparent basal mismatch at 16:00 is deliberately left unchanged, because raising it would also increase automation aggressiveness immediately before the hours that already carry the most hypoglycemia.

The 5.935 U of insulin on board recorded at the end of the data on 08-21 at 22:09 local, at 245 mg/dL with a further 2.12 U requested and no subsequent readings in the package, should be raised with the care team as a specific example rather than treated as a historical curiosity.

This appears to be a customized AAPS build containing logic that is not present in the supplied settings inventory, including UAM boost behavior that exceeded the configured SMB limits and effective targets below the profile floor. Any change should be validated against the documentation for this specific build, because standard AAPS guidance may not describe its behavior accurately.

Rescue carbohydrate is not recorded anywhere in this period, so the depth, duration and recovery of the hypoglycemic episodes cannot be verified from the data, and the true low burden may differ from what the CGM statistics suggest in either direction.

Recorded device events, including the occlusion and pump error on 08-19 and three site changes, may have affected insulin delivery on specific days. Where a pattern coincides with such an event, the event should be considered before any therapy setting is blamed.

If severe or unexplained hypoglycemia, loss of hypoglycemia awareness, or repeated pump or infusion-set problems occur, contact the diabetes care team promptly rather than continuing with self-directed adjustments.
